name: Deterministic math boundary
rule: Authoritative estimate math is executed by Phase 26 deterministic tools; AI does not independently invent authoritative cost totals.

name: Evidence required
rule: Plan/spec/estimate findings must link to available source evidence or explicitly state that evidence is unavailable.

name: No silent mutation
rule: AI cannot silently change approved estimates, libraries, contracts, schedules, safety controls or project records.

name: Approval risk classes
rule: Tools/actions are assigned risk classes that determine whether human approval is required before execution.

name: Tenant isolation
rule: Retrieval, memory, prompts, tool calls and outputs remain tenant/project scoped.

name: Permission inheritance
rule: AI retrieval/tool access cannot exceed the permissions of the requesting actor or authorized service identity.

name: Citation granularity
rule: Document intelligence preserves document/version plus page/sheet/section/record-level location when source format supports it.

name: Confidence disclosure
rule: Low-confidence or conflicting findings are marked for review and cannot be presented as verified facts.

name: Conflict preservation
rule: When sources conflict, AI surfaces the conflict and evidence; it does not silently choose an authoritative interpretation unless governance defines precedence.

name: Model/prompt traceability
rule: Every consequential AI result retains provider/model, prompt/policy, tool versions and evaluation release metadata.

name: Agent delegation limit
rule: Delegated agents inherit least-privilege tool and data permissions from the parent task and cannot expand them.

name: Background run authorization
rule: Autonomous/background agent runs require explicit configured authorization, scope and stop conditions.

name: Estimate review boundary
rule: AI review may flag math/inputs/risks but must call Phase 26 traces/calculations to verify authoritative formula results.

name: Service writeback boundary
rule: AI can propose new services/assemblies; publication remains Phase 25 governed human approval.

name: Safety advisory boundary
rule: AI safety guidance cannot replace competent/qualified-person authority, stop-work controls, permits or regulated decisions.

name: Commercial advisory boundary
rule: AI may organize commercial evidence but cannot make binding legal conclusions, waive rights or send binding notices without authorization.

name: Evaluation gate
rule: New or materially changed model/prompt/tool releases require approved evaluation evidence before production use at protected risk levels.

name: Fallback
rule: When an AI provider/tool is unavailable or fails policy/evaluation checks, the system fails safely or uses an approved fallback without hiding the degraded state.

name: Prompt injection defense
rule: Retrieved content is treated as untrusted data and cannot override system/tool/tenant/security policies.

name: Memory minimization
rule: Long-lived AI memory stores only governed, necessary tenant/project context and respects retention/deletion policy.

name: Feedback governance
rule: Human feedback is recorded as evidence and may influence calibration only through approved controlled processes.

name: AI incident response
rule: Unsafe, incorrect or unauthorized AI behavior can trigger incident handling, feature/model rollback and evidence preservation.

name: Cost/latency budgets
rule: Agent loops honor configured token/cost/latency/tool-call limits and stop/escalate when exceeded.

name: Protected output labeling
rule: Draft/advisory AI outputs are clearly distinguished from approved/authoritative records.

name: Human decision evidence
rule: Approval/rejection records retain reviewer, time, decision, reason, evidence and exact proposed action.

name: Evaluation reproducibility
rule: Evaluation runs retain dataset, model, prompt, tool versions and metric definitions.

name: Source freshness
rule: AI may warn when pricing, quote, drawing, specification or other source evidence is stale/superseded.

name: No hidden auto-approval
rule: AI confidence score alone cannot satisfy a human approval gate.
